ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\square ABCD$, $AB=13$, $AD=5$, and $AC\perp BC$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw DE $\perp$ BC, intersecting the extended line of BC at E,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
therefore BC=AD=5, AD$\parallel$BC,\\
since $AC\perp BC$,\\
therefore $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $AC= \sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{13^{2}-5^{2}}=12$,\\
since DE$\perp$BC,\\
therefore AC$\parallel$DE,\\
therefore quadrilateral ACED is a parallelogram,\\
therefore CE=AD=5, DE=AC=12,\\
therefore BE=BC+CE=10,\\
since DE$\perp$BC,\\
therefore, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $BD= \sqrt{BE^{2}+DE^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}+10^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{61}}$.
